metadata.title: Motive raises $1.3 billion from General Catalyst

content.text:
Motive announced Thursday it secured more than $1.3 billion in growth financing from General Catalyst and withdrew its previously filed S-1. The San Francisco-based company reported its annual recurring revenue crossed $600 million, the company's strongest quarter. ARR growth accelerated to 30% year over year.
ARR from customers spending more than $100,000 grew nearly 60% year over year. Net revenue retention for these customers was above 120%.
Pranav Singhvi, a managing director at General Catalyst, joined Motive's board.
Growth financing after record ARR
Motive said the capital will fuel AI investment across the platform and grow its sales, support, and service teams.The raise pays for heads in the field as much as it pays for new models. Earlier this year the company named Thomas Hansen, a veteran of Amplitude, UiPath, Dropbox, and Microsoft, as its first president of go-to-market.
Motive serves nearly 100,000 customers, from small fleets to Fortune 500 operators. Those accounts span trucking, construction, energy, field service, manufacturing, agriculture, and related industries.
S-1 withdrawn
Motive said the financing allowed it to pull the S-1 and keep a public listing as a later path.
"With this financing, we're very well capitalized. We withdrew our previously filed S-1," Motive Co-founder and CEO Shoaib Makani told FreightWaves. "But we remain very well positioned for the public markets in the future. Motive has the operational capacity and the growth profile, to be a public company. With this financing we can continue to operate privately, but with the resources to invest aggressively."
Motive already counts more than a million commercial vehicles on its platform, by Makani's figure, against a North American ballpark he puts at 30 million. He called that a 3% penetration rate.
"The TAM here is hundreds of billions of dollars, and we're just scratching the surface," Makani said.
Motive's chief financial officer tied the same check to product work and a larger sales force.
"From our earliest conversations, it was clear that General Catalyst shares our long-term vision for building Motive into a generational business," said Chirag Shah. "Our momentum has never been stronger, and this financing will allow us to compound that for years to come through continued cutting-edge product innovation and scaling our go-to-market engine."
Bringing AI to physical operations
Motive has shipped AI-powered cameras since 2017 that flag phone use, fatigue, and following distance. Makani said less than 20% of commercial vehicles have one, even when he puts the return at several times the hardware cost. The company said the raise will expand new products like its newly launched Maintenance and Operations Intelligence.
